# AgentScope Go

[CI](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope-go/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[Go](go.mod)
[License](LICENSE)

[Español](README.es-ES.md) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Examples](#examples) · [Documentation](#documentation) · [Contributing](#contributing)

AgentScope Go is a Go library for building LLM applications with agents, tools
and multi-agent workflows. It implements the core concepts of
[AgentScope](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope) through Go interfaces,
contexts and channels, and can be embedded in a service or command-line program.

## What you can build

- **Tool-using assistants:** connect model calls to Go functions, manage context
  and request human confirmation for tool execution. Use [AskUser](docs/tools.md#askuser)
  to collect structured choices through your own frontend. On `main` (unreleased),
  opt into [bounded tool dispatch](docs/tools.md#bounded-tool-dispatch-experimental)
  with `agent.WithToolConcurrencyLimit(width)`.
- **Multi-agent workflows:** coordinate agents with pipelines, message routing
  and leader/worker teams. On `main` (unreleased), use the experimental
  [TeamPipeline](docs/team-pipeline.md) for serial named-member delegation
  and participant confirmation/external-result routing.
- **Applications with memory:** combine retrieval, conversation state and memory
  middleware with your own data sources.
- **Services and experiments:** expose an HTTP service or browser UI, record
  model responses, evaluate runs and inspect traces.

## Quick start

You need **Go 1.25+** and, for the program below, an Anthropic API key and an
available model ID. Other adapters are listed under [Model providers](#model-providers).

### Install in your application

Install the latest tagged release from the community module path. Applications
using `github.com/alanfokco/agentscope-go/v2` need to update their import prefix;
see the [module migration notes](CHANGELOG.md#changed--repository-and-module-path-move).

From a new directory:

```bash
mkdir agentscope-demo
cd agentscope-demo
go mod init example.com/agentscope-demo
go get github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope-go/v2@latest
```

### Create an agent

Save this as `main.go`:

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"os"
	"time"

	"github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope-go/v2/pkg/agentscope/agent"
	"github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope-go/v2/pkg/agentscope/model"
)

func main() {
	cm, err := model.NewAnthropicChatModel(&model.AnthropicConfig{
		SecretAPIKey:    model.NewSecretStr(os.Getenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")),
		Model:           os.Getenv("ANTHROPIC_MODEL"),
		MaxOutputTokens: 1024,
	})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	assistant := agent.NewUnifiedAgent(
		"assistant", "You are a helpful assistant. Keep answers concise.", cm,
	)

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), time.Minute)
	defer cancel()

	reply, err := assistant.Reply(ctx, "What is an AI agent? Explain in one sentence.")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	if text := reply.GetTextContent("\n"); text != nil {
		fmt.Println(*text)
	}
}
```

Set your key and a model ID available to your account, then run the program.
These shell commands use Bash/Zsh syntax; in PowerShell, set environment variables
with `$env:NAME = 'value'`.

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='your-api-key'
export ANTHROPIC_MODEL='your-model-id'
go mod tidy
go run .
```

The program makes a model API request and prints its reply. To add function
calling, see [the tool example](examples/agent_v2/); for configuration and next
steps, see [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md).

## Model providers

Adapters are available for **OpenAI** (Chat Completions and Responses),
**Anthropic**, **DashScope**, **DeepSeek**, **Gemini**, **Moonshot**, **xAI** and
**Ollama**. See [provider configuration](docs/model-providers.md) and the
[adapter source](pkg/agentscope/model/) for options and defaults.

Tool calling, multimodal input, thinking and usage reporting depend on the
provider and model. Provider `ChatStream` methods expose response chunks;
`UnifiedAgent.ReplyStream` streams thinking/text deltas from `ChatStream` by
default when no middleware is installed. Legacy middleware chains keep buffered
`Chat` calls so response filters can run before publication. Use
`agent.WithModelStreaming(false)` for the previous buffered behavior. See
[agent streaming](docs/streaming.md) for completion, cancellation and fallback
semantics.

For local models, configure the context window and request timeout for your
server and device. Model cards describe model capabilities; they do not configure
the server. See [edge deployment](docs/edge-deployment.md) and
[the tracked local-model limitations](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope-go/issues/8).

## Examples

Examples run from a repository checkout, separately from the application above.
This worker-pool demo uses simulated jobs and needs no model API key:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope-go.git
cd agentscope-go
go run ./examples/agent_pool
```

Start with [agent_v2](examples/agent_v2/) for function tools,
[model_call](examples/model_call/) for direct model streaming, or
[webui](examples/webui/) for a browser interface. Check each example's source for
its model choice, environment variables and required services or runtimes.

# LazyLLM: A  Low-code Development Tool For Building Multi-agent LLMs Applications.
[中文](README.CN.md) |  [EN](README.md)

[CI](https://github.com/LazyAGI/LazyLLM/actions/workflows/main.yml)
[License](https://opensource.org/license/apache-2-0)
[GitHub star chart](https://star-history.com/#LazyAGI/LazyLLM)
[](https://discord.gg/cDSrRycuM6)

## What is LazyLLM?

LazyLLM is a low-code development tool for building **multi-agent** large language model applications. It assists developers in creating complex AI applications at very low costs and enables continuous iterative optimization. LazyLLM offers a convenient workflow for application building and provides numerous standard processes and tools for various stages of the application development process.
The AI application development process based on LazyLLM follows **prototype building -> data feedback -> iterative optimization**, which means you can quickly build a prototype application using LazyLLM, then analyze bad cases using task-specific data, and subsequently iterate on algorithms and fine-tune models at critical stages of the application to gradually improve the overall application performance.
LazyLLM is committed to the unity of agility and efficiency. Developers can efficiently iterate algorithms and then apply the iterated algorithms to industrial production, supporting multiple users, fault tolerance, and high concurrency.
**User Documentation**： https://docs.lazyllm.ai/
Scan the QR code below with WeChat to join the group chat(left) or learn more by watching a video(right)

## Features

**Convenient AI Application Assembly Process**: Even if you are not familiar with large models, you can still easily assemble AI applications with multiple agents using our built-in data flow and functional modules, just like Lego building.

**One-Click Deployment of Complex Applications**: We offer the capability to deploy all modules with a single click. Specifically, during the POC (Proof of Concept) phase, LazyLLM simplifies the deployment process of multi-agent applications through a lightweight gateway mechanism, solving the problem of sequentially starting each submodule service (such as LLM, Embedding, etc.) and configuring URLs, making the entire process smoother and more efficient. In the application release phase, LazyLLM provides the ability to package images with one click, making it easy to utilize Kubernetes' gateway, load balancing, and fault tolerance capabilities.

**Cross-Platform Compatibility**: Switch IaaS platforms with one click without modifying code, compatible with bare-metal servers, development machines, Slurm clusters, public clouds, etc. This allows developed applications to be seamlessly migrated to other IaaS platforms, greatly reducing the workload of code modification.

**Unified User Experience for Different Technical Choices**: We provide a unified user experience for online models from different service providers and locally deployed models, allowing developers to freely switch and upgrade their models for experimentation. In addition, we also unify the user experience for mainstream inference frameworks, fine-tuning frameworks, relational databases, vector databases, and document databases.

**Efficient Model Fine-Tuning**: Support fine-tuning models within applications to continuously improve application performance. Automatically select the best fine-tuning framework and model splitting strategy based on the fine-tuning scenario. This not only simplifies the maintenance of model iterations but also allows algorithm researchers to focus more on algorithm and data iteration, without handling tedious engineering tasks.

## What can you build with Lazyllm

LazyLLM can be used to build common artificial intelligence applications. Here are some examples.

### 3.1 ChatBots

**This is a simple example of a chat bot.**

```python
# set environment variable: LAZYLLM_OPENAI_API_KEY=xx
# or you can make a config file(~/.lazyllm/config.json) and add openai_api_key=xx
import lazyllm
chat = lazyllm.OnlineChatModule()
lazyllm.WebModule(chat).start().wait()
```

If you want to use a locally deployed model, please ensure you have installed at least one inference framework (lightllm or vllm), and then use the following code

```python
import lazyllm
# Model will be downloaded automatically if you have an internet connection.
chat = lazyllm.TrainableModule('internlm2-chat-7b')
lazyllm.WebModule(chat, port=23466).start().wait()
```

If you installed `lazyllm` using `pip` and ensured that the `bin` directory of your Python environment is in your `$PATH`, you can quickly start a chatbot by executing `lazyllm run chatbot`. If you want to use a local model, you need to specify the model name with the `--model` parameter. For example, you can start a chatbot based on a local model by using `lazyllm run chatbot --model=internlm2-chat-7b`.

**This is an advanced bot example with multimodality and intent recognition.**

Demo Multimodal bot

 click to look up prompts and imports

```python
from lazyllm import TrainableModule, WebModule, deploy, pipeline
from lazyllm.tools import IntentClassifier

painter_prompt = 'Now you are a master of drawing prompts, capable of converting any Chinese content entered by the user into English drawing prompts. In this task, you need to convert any input content into English drawing prompts, and you can enrich and expand the prompt content.'
musician_prompt = 'Now you are a master of music composition prompts, capable of converting any Chinese content entered by the user into English music composition prompts. In this task, you need to convert any input content into English music composition prompts, and you can enrich and expand the prompt content.'
```

```python
base = TrainableModule('internlm2-chat-7b')
with IntentClassifier(base) as ic:
    ic.case['Chat', base]
    ic.case['Speech Recognition', TrainableModule('SenseVoiceSmall')]
    ic.case['Image QA', TrainableModule('InternVL3_5-1B').deploy_method(deploy.LMDeploy)]
    ic.case['Drawing', pipeline(base.share().prompt(painter_prompt), TrainableModule('stable-diffusion-3-medium'))]
    ic.case['Generate Music', pipeline(base.share().prompt(musician_prompt), TrainableModule('musicgen-small'))]
    ic.case['Text to Speech', TrainableModule('ChatTTS')]
WebModule(ic, history=[base], audio=True, port=8847).start().wait()
```

### 3.2 Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Demo RAG

 Click to view imports and prompt

```python

import os
import lazyllm
from lazyllm import pipeline, parallel, bind, SentenceSplitter, Document, Retriever, Reranker

prompt = 'You will play the role of an AI Q&A assistant and complete a dialogue task. In this task, you need to provide your answer based on the given context and question.'
```

This is an online deployment example:

```python
documents = Document(dataset_path="your data path", embed=lazyllm.OnlineEmbeddingModule(), manager=False)
documents.create_node_group(name="sentences", transform=SentenceSplitter, chunk_size=1024, chunk_overlap=100)
with pipeline() as ppl:
    with parallel().sum as ppl.prl:
        prl.retriever1 = Retriever(documents, group_name="sentences", similarity="cosine", topk=3)
        prl.retriever2 = Retriever(documents, "CoarseChunk", "bm25_chinese", 0.003, topk=3)

    ppl.reranker = Reranker("ModuleReranker", model="bge-reranker-large", topk=1) | bind(query=ppl.input)
    ppl.formatter = (lambda nodes, query: dict(context_str="".join([node.get_content() for node in nodes]), query=query)) | bind(query=ppl.input)
    ppl.llm = lazyllm.OnlineChatModule(stream=False).prompt(lazyllm.ChatPrompter(prompt, extra_keys=["context_str"]))

lazyllm.WebModule(ppl, port=23466).start().wait()
```

Here is an example of a local deployment:

```python
documents = Document(dataset_path='/file/to/yourpath', embed=lazyllm.TrainableModule('bge-large-zh-v1.5'))
documents.create_node_group(name="sentences", transform=SentenceSplitter, chunk_size=1024, chunk_overlap=100)

with pipeline() as ppl:
    with parallel().sum as ppl.prl:
        prl.retriever1 = Retriever(documents, group_name="sentences", similarity="cosine", topk=3)
        prl.retriever2 = Retriever(documents, "CoarseChunk", "bm25_chinese", 0.003, topk=3)

    ppl.reranker = Reranker("ModuleReranker", model="bge-reranker-large", topk=1) | bind(query=ppl.input)
    ppl.formatter = (lambda nodes, query: dict(context_str="".join([node.get_content() for node in nodes]), query=query)) | bind(query=ppl.input)
    ppl.llm = lazyllm.TrainableModule("internlm2-chat-7b").prompt(lazyllm.ChatPrompter(prompt, extra_keys=["context_str"]))

lazyllm.WebModule(ppl, port=23456).start().wait()
```

If you installed `lazyllm` using `pip` and ensured that the `bin` directory of your Python environment is in your `$PATH`, you can quickly start a retrieval-augmented bot by executing `lazyllm run rag --documents=/file/to/yourpath`. If you want to use a local model, you need to specify the model name with the `--model` parameter. For example, you can start a retrieval-augmented bot based on a local model by using `lazyllm run rag --documents=/file/to/yourpath --model=internlm2-chat-7b`.

### 3.3 More Examples

For more examples, please refer to our official documentation [Usage Examples](https://docs.lazyllm.ai/en/stable/Cookbook/chatbot/)
* [Painting Master](https://docs.lazyllm.ai/en/stable/Cookbook/painting_master/)
* [Multimodal Chatbot](https://docs.lazyllm.ai/en/stable/Cookbook/multimodal_robot/)
* [Knowledge Base](https://docs.lazyllm.ai/en/stable/Cookbook/rag/)
* [Search Agent](https://docs.lazyllm.ai/en/latest/Cookbook/bocha_search/)
* [API Interaction Agent](https://docs.lazyllm.ai/en/latest/Cookbook/API_Interaction_Agent_demo/)
* [Tool-Calling Intelligent Agent](https://docs.lazyllm.ai/en/latest/Cookbook/flex_agent/)

## What can LazyLLM do

1. **Application Building**: Defines workflows such as pipeline, parallel, diverter, if, switch, and loop. Developers can quickly build multi-agent AI applications based on any functions and modules. Supports one-click deployment for assembled multi-agent applications, and also supports partial or complete updates to the applications.
2. **Platform-independent**: Consistent user experience across different computing platforms. Currently compatible with various platforms such as bare metal, Slurm, SenseCore, etc.
3. **Supports fine-tuning and inference for large models**:
    * Offline (local) model services:
        + Supports fine-tuning frameworks: collie, peft
        + Supports inference frameworks: lightllm, vllm
        + Supports automatically selecting the most suitable framework and model parameters (such as micro-bs, tp, zero, etc.) based on user scenarios..
    * Online services:
        + Supports fine-tuning services: GPT, SenseNova, Tongyi Qianwen
        + Supports inference services: GPT, SenseNova, Kimi, Zhipu, Tongyi Qianwen
        + Supports embedding inference services: OpenAI, SenseNova, GLM, Tongyi Qianwen
    * Support developers to use local services and online services uniformly.
4. **Supports common RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) components**: Document, Parser, Retriever, Reranker, etc.
5. **Supports basic webs**: such as chat interface and document management interface, etc.

## Installation

### pip installation (recommended)

To install only lazyllm and necessary dependencies, you can use:
```bash
pip3 install lazyllm
```

To install lazyllm and all dependencies, you can use:
```bash
pip3 install lazyllm
lazyllm install full
```

### Installation from source

```bash
git clone git@github.com:LazyAGI/LazyLLM.git
cd LazyLLM
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### Installation on Windows or macOS

For installation on Windows or macOS, please refer to our [tutorial](https://docs.lazyllm.ai/zh-cn/stable/Home/environment)

# Mika

**An AI assistant on your phone: say what you need, and it works your apps and the web until it's done.**

It works on a hidden background screen, so you can keep using your phone.

English · [简体中文](docs/readme/README.zh-CN.md) · [繁體中文](docs/readme/README.zh-Hant.md) · [日本語](docs/readme/README.ja.md) · [한국어](docs/readme/README.ko.md) · [Español](docs/readme/README.es.md)

 "Send a message to File Transfer": Mika's chat on the left, each step on its background screen on the right (4× speed; chat list blurred)

## Get things done with one sentence

   "What did the group talk about today?"   Scrolls through the chat in the background, then sums it up
   "A charger under $30, rated 4.5 stars or more"   Adds the pick to the cart and stops before checkout
   "What has this creator posted lately?"   Opens the app, reads post by post, then sums it up

 More demos

  Greets recruiters for 3 jobs on a job site
  Finds the cheapest nonstop from San Francisco to New York
  Reads out the top 5 stories on a news site

  Finds jobs and greets recruiters
  Watches ads to unlock music perks
  Orders takeout with stacked discounts, asks before paying

 Several demos use apps popular in China: WeChat is the main messaging app there, and Xiaohongshu (RED) is a lifestyle and social platform. Mika isn't tied to them; it works with any app or website on your phone.

## Why Mika

| | |
|---|---|
| 📱 **Leaves your screen alone** | Opens apps, taps, types and scrolls on a separate background screen while you use your phone as usual; tap the small live view whenever you want to watch |
| 🧩 **Works with any app** | Looks at the screen and finds buttons the way a person does: no app APIs, no per-app integration |
| 🌐 **Call it from any web page** | In the built-in browser, say what you want on the page you're reading and it works right there; touch the page and it stops |
| 🧠 **Gets better with use** | Remembers the preferences you tell it, and turns tasks it finishes into skills so next time is faster and steadier |
| 🔒 **Your data stays on your phone** | There is no Mika server; use your own model API key, or sign in with a ChatGPT, xAI or OpenRouter account |
| 🆓 **Open source and free** | Apache-2.0, all code public |

## Get started in three steps

1. **Install**: download the APK from [Releases](https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/releases/latest).
2. **Connect a model**: in Settings › Model, pick a provider and enter an API key, or just sign in with an account ([models and sign-in](docs/models.en.md)).
3. **To operate phone apps**: follow the "Set up phone control" wizard in Settings and pair wireless debugging on the phone once ([setup guide](docs/setup-guide.en.md)). Skip this if you only want chat, web and files.

Then try saying: "Set alarms for 9:40 and 10:00 tomorrow morning" or "Check the weather at 8 every morning and tell me only if it will rain".

> 💡 Have a computer handy? Send this to the AI agent on it and it will set everything up for you:
> `Follow https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/blob/main/docs/install-with-agent.en.md to install Mika on the Android phone connected over USB.`

## What it can do

| | |
|---|---|
| **Operate apps** | Reads long lists and chat histories, taps and types, shares text into apps; hands logins, verification codes and payments to you |
| **Browse the web** | A built-in desktop-class browser that keeps you signed in, reads pages, downloads and uploads; paces itself and hands block pages to you |
| **Your current screen** | Double-tap the floating capsule to send the screen you're looking at: "how should I reply?", "note this down" |

## 🏛️ Executive Summary & Architectural Highlights

**AVault** is an open-source, security-focused telecommunications management platform and cryptographic voice vault designed for modern Android devices (Android 12 to Android 16+).

Traditional call recording utilities store raw audio in unencrypted `.mp3` or `.m4a` files within shared public storage directories, exposing sensitive voice communications to third-party apps with media reading permissions, media indexers, and unauthenticated physical extraction.

AVault solves this paradigm by pairing **rootless system telecom integration** (via privileged ADB shell Binder IPC) with **hardware-backed AES-256-GCM encryption**, **zero-plaintext ephemeral playback**, **multi-factor biometric authentication**, and **automated lifecycle retention management**.

### Core Pillars
1. **Hardware-Isolated Master Keys:** Cryptographic keys are generated inside the device's hardware security module (TEE / StrongBox Keymaster) via the Android KeyStore Provider. Raw key material never enters user-space RAM.
2. **Zero-Plaintext Ephemeral Playback:** Decryption occurs on-the-fly directly in volatile memory into an isolated POSIX file descriptor (`0600` access) with `.nomedia` indexing suppression. The temporary stream is cryptographically shredded the millisecond playback halts.
3. **Multi-Factor Application Lock:** Enforces biometric authentication (Fingerprint, Face Unlock, Device Credential) backed by a salted PBKDF2/SHA-256 PIN engine with exponential brute-force backoff protection.
4. **Automated Storage Lifecycle & Retention:** Automatically prunes expired non-bookmarked recordings after a configurable interval (1d to 1y), while bookmarked calls remain permanently preserved and immune to cleanup.
5. **Stealth & Minimalist Presentation:** Suppresses call-end toast notifications and uses discreet status alerts (`"Started"`, `"Saved"`), paired with `FLAG_SECURE` to prevent screen scraping, screenshots, and task-switcher previews.

## 🔐 Binary Format & Cryptographic Specification

Every recording managed by AVault is packaged into a proprietary, tamper-resistant binary container format: `.vault`.

### 1. `.vault` Container Structure

```text
+-------------------+--------------------+------------------------+------------------------------------+------------------------+
|  Magic Identifier |   Format Version   |  Initialization Vector |        Ciphertext Payload          |   Authentication Tag   |
|   (0x00 - 0x03)   |       (0x04)       |     (0x05 - 0x10)      |        (0x11 - EOF-16)             |       (EOF-15 - EOF)   |
|      4 Bytes      |       1 Byte       |        12 Bytes        |            Variable                |        16 Bytes        |
+-------------------+--------------------+------------------------+------------------------------------+------------------------+
|   "AVLT" (ASCII)  |    0x01 (UINT8)    |   CSPRNG Nonce (GCM)   |   Encrypted Opus/AAC Audio Stream  |   GCM Auth Tag (128b)  |
+-------------------+--------------------+------------------------+------------------------------------+------------------------+
```

- **Magic Identifier (Bytes 0–3):** `0x41 0x56 0x4C 0x54` (`"AVLT"`). Verifies container integrity and distinguishes valid encrypted containers from malformed files.
- **Format Version (Byte 4):** `0x01`. Enables backward-compatible cryptographic migrations.
- **Initialization Vector (Bytes 5–16):** 12-byte (96-bit) cryptographically secure random nonce generated uniquely per recording session via `java.security.SecureRandom`. An IV is never reused.
- **Ciphertext Payload (Bytes 17 to EOF-16):** Audio bitstream compressed via Opus (default, 32–128 kbps) or AAC, encrypted using AES-256 in Galois/Counter Mode.
- **Authentication Tag (Final 16 Bytes):** 128-bit Galois Authentication Tag. Guarantees message integrity; any ciphertext modification or bit-flipping causes decryption failure before playback begins.

### 2. Key Management & Derivation Parameters
- **Master Encryption Key:** Generated within the Android KeyStore provider (`AndroidKeyStore`), algorithm `AES/GCM/NoPadding`, 256-bit key length, bound to the app's UID.
- **PIN Hashing:** PBKDF2 with HMAC-SHA256, 128-bit cryptographic salt, 100,000 iterations.
- **Lockout Policy:** 5 consecutive incorrect unlock attempts trigger a 30-second exponential hardware lockout.

Kikumap

  English  ·  简体中文

   A mind map for your Claude and ChatGPT chats.
  See which chats are running and which are waiting for you, from the menu bar or your desktop.
  Sort them into a map. Take them with you.

  ⬇︎ Download for macOS

   Website  ·
   Features  ·
   Install  ·
   Privacy  ·
   FAQ  ·
   Support ❤️

You pinned a dozen chats in Claude, and a few Codex chats in ChatGPT. One is planning your trip, one is fixing a test, one finished ten minutes ago and you haven't looked. **Kikumap** sits in your menu bar and keeps track of both: what's running, what's done, what needs your OK. Open it and your pinned chats are laid out as a mind map that you arrange, MindNode-style. A desktop widget shows the same at a glance, with your Claude and ChatGPT usage.

**Native and featherlight.** Swift and AppKit only: no Electron, no web view, no helper processes, no third-party code (its line icons are from [Lucide](https://lucide.dev), ISC). A small download that mostly waits for changes (with a light check every half minute), and stops drawing entirely when its window is hidden.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/abd1dc24-4bc4-433a-8bf0-ad95262d4902

> [!NOTE]
> **Good to know.** The Claude app has no public API, so Kikumap reads its window through macOS Accessibility; ChatGPT's threads come from the files its desktop app keeps on your Mac. When either app changes, parts of Kikumap may stop working until it's updated. Kikumap is an independent project, not made by or affiliated with Anthropic or OpenAI.

## Features

### Know what Claude and ChatGPT are doing

One icon in the menu bar. The orange flower spins while a pinned chat is running. A red badge counts chats that finished and you haven't read, with **!** when one needs your approval.

**Hear it instead of checking.** A sound plays when a chat finishes or needs you, and Kikumap can then say which one ("Pricing plan is done") in the voice, speed and words you choose. Or use your own sound file.

Works with the Claude desktop app, Claude Code (Terminal, VS Code, the app's Code mode) and the ChatGPT desktop app. From ChatGPT, Kikumap shows the chats that run on your Mac: the **Codex** chats you pin in the ChatGPT app (pinned threads and the threads in pinned projects) show next to Claude's, marked **GPT**, in ChatGPT's order, and running and unread follow ChatGPT's own dots. Codex sessions in VS Code or the terminal show like Claude Code sessions: while they run, while unread, and for 12 hours after. Ordinary ChatGPT chats are kept online, not on your Mac, so they can't show, pinned or not. Nothing to set up: Kikumap reads what ChatGPT keeps on your Mac.

### Your chats, as a map

The left column mirrors the chats you pinned in Claude and the Codex chats you pinned in ChatGPT, **in each app's order**, and your Claude Code sessions. The map starts empty: nothing goes on it until you put it there. Drag them onto your own topics. While you drag, the item rides a live branch and the rest of the map slides aside to show where it will land. The map never rearranges itself on its own.

**Several at once:** drag a box on empty space (or ⌘/⇧-click), or ⌘/⇧-click in the left column, then drag any one of them. They all come along, in order. Hold space and move the mouse, or swipe with two fingers, to move around the map. The left column and the timeline can be hidden (⌃⌘S, ⌃⌘T) or resized by dragging their edge, and ⌘+ / ⌘- make everything in the window bigger or smaller.

Real conversations carry a small orange mark, so they stand apart from plain topics. Hover one for two buttons: open it in Claude or ChatGPT, or mark it unread again (⇧⌘U) so it waits for you until you've opened it.

### Make it yours

Right-click any topic for a branch colour and a shape: square, circle, triangle, diamond, cross or star. Colours flow down the branch, into the timeline and the menu.

### Tag anything

Tags like *In progress*, *Waiting on others* or *Slides*. Pick them from the right-click menu, or drag one from the shelf straight onto a chat.

Click a tag to highlight everything that has it; the rest of the map fades back. Click again to clear.

### Keyboard-first

Like a real mind-map app: ⇥ new subtopic, ⏎ sibling, ⌥↑↓ reorder, ⌘Z undo. Also ⌫ delete, ⌥. fold, ⌘F search, and ⌘↓ (or a tap on space) to open a chat in its app, as in Finder.

### What ran, and what's next

The timeline shows when Claude and ChatGPT worked on each chat, in your branch colours; chats running at the same time get rows of their own. Drag ahead to see your scheduled tasks (with usage turned on), each with a live countdown. Click anything to open it.

### Take everything with you

Tick topics and export every chat under them, pinned or not, one folder per chat:

- `memory.md`: a hand-off summary Claude writes inside the chat
- `prompts.md` and `conversation.md`
- `artifacts/` and `attachments/`

The export can keep itself up to date. **Import** starts a new pinned chat per folder (in a new Claude account, say), with the summary and the artifacts attached, so you pick up where you left off.

### On your desktop  new

A widget for the desktop or Notification Center, in three sizes. Running and unread chats on top; then your usage, Claude's (the 5-hour session and the week), ChatGPT's, or both, each row marked with whose it is; and below, the last 24 hours as bars, a colour per chat. Click a chat to open it.

Right-click the desktop → **Edit Widgets** and search for Kikumap. macOS 14 or later.

### How much got done  new

How long Claude and ChatGPT worked, split by chat, in bars of 1, 3, 6, 12, 24 or 48 hours over the last 7, 14, 30 or 90 days. Hover for the details, click a segment to open the chat. View → Statistics (⌘Y), or the chart button at the top of the window.

### And a lot more

   Finished chats light up  A chat that's done but unread turns solid on the map, with a red dot.
   Find anything  ⌘F searches topics, chats and tags; ⏎ jumps to the next match.

   Your day at a glance  Which chats Claude and ChatGPT worked on today, and for how long, in the menu.
   Usage in the menu  This session and this week, like claude.ai, plus what's scheduled next.

   The map as a PDF  The whole map on one light page, ready to print or share.
   Daily backups  A copy of your map every day, before your first change.

   Light or dark  Follows your Mac, or flip it with the moon.
   English · 中文  Every label, menu and tag in either language.

## What it can and can't see

Kikumap reads what the apps keep on this Mac. It never signs in to your accounts; with usage on, it asks Anthropic only for your usage and your scheduled tasks' times, using the sign-in Claude Code keeps here.

| Shows | Doesn't show |
|---|---|
| Chats you pin in Claude, wherever you started them (pins sync from your phone and the web), while the Claude desktop app runs on this Mac | Chats you haven't pinned; Claude used only in a browser or on another device, with no Claude app running here |
| Claude Code sessions run on this Mac: Terminal, VS Code, Cursor, the Claude app's Code mode (once its hooks are connected) | Claude Code running on another computer or a server: over SSH, in VS Code Remote or a dev container, or in the cloud (its hooks run there, not here) |
| Codex chats you pin in the ChatGPT desktop app, and Codex sessions in VS Code or the terminal on this Mac | Ordinary ChatGPT chats (kept online), Codex on another computer or a server, Codex cloud tasks |
| Claude's scheduled tasks, by name and run times, on the timeline (with usage on) | What a scheduled or cloud task does while it runs |
| Claude's usage, through the sign-in Claude Code keeps on this Mac (a Claude subscription); ChatGPT's, from its own files | Usage of an API key billed per use, or of an account not signed in on this Mac |

Running and finished come from this Mac too: Claude's sidebar while its window is open on the desktop you're using, Claude Code's hooks, and ChatGPT's files. With Full Disk Access, and Claude's notifications allowed in macOS, Claude's notifications add when it needs your approval or an answer, and when a Cowork task in the Claude app finishes; Claude sends none when an ordinary chat's reply finishes. (Code sessions in the app come through the Claude Code connection.) The intro shows this as a picture.

## Install

**[Download Kikumap.dmg](https://github.com/tang1693/KIKUmap/releases/latest/download/Kikumap.dmg)** (Apple silicon and Intel, macOS 13 or later), open it and drag **Kikumap** to **Applications**.

The first time you open it, macOS says it can't check the app, because it isn't signed with a paid Apple Developer ID:

1. In that message, click **Done** (not *Move to Trash*), then open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**.
2. Scroll down and click **Open Anyway** next to Kikumap. (On macOS 13–14 you can also right-click the app → Open.)
3. A short intro asks for one permission, Accessibility, so Kikumap can look at the Claude app's chat list. Everything else is optional. On its last page you can have Kikumap open when you log in (change it any time in Settings → General).
4. **Pin the chats you want to follow.** Kikumap follows pinned chats (and Claude Code and Codex sessions): pin a chat in Claude, or a Codex chat in ChatGPT, and it shows in the menu, the left column and the widget.

Keep the Claude app's sidebar open, on Chat, with its Pinned section unfolded. ChatGPT needs nothing: Kikumap reads what its desktop app keeps on your Mac. To remove Kikumap later: first turn off Settings → General → *Start at login* and, if you connected it, click Settings → Access → *Disconnect Claude Code*; then drag the app to the Trash.

  Build from source

Needs the Xcode Command Line Tools (macOS offers to install them).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/tang1693/KIKUmap.git
cd KIKUmap
open Install.command        # or double-click it in Finder
```

`Install.command` builds with `swiftc` (Swift 5.10 or later), installs to `~/Applications` and asks whether to start at login. It signs the app with a certificate it creates once in your login keychain, so the permissions you grant survive later rebuilds. `scripts/build-release.sh` builds the universal disk image.

# HelixHarness

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

> **Built to Adapt. Designed to Evolve.**
>
> Your team's engineering DNA, carried into AI development.

**HelixHarness helps your team build its own AI coding harness on Codex and Claude Code.** It brings your business knowledge, engineering rules and development workflow into the agent's work—from requirements through implementation, tests, review and archive. Verified lessons stay with the project, ready for the next feature.

Start with the plugin. When you want to improve the harness itself, the optional **helixharness-platform** lets maintainers observe usage, compare framework versions and evaluate candidate improvements before adopting them.

**9 commands · Codex / Claude Code · Single repo / multi-repo Workspace · Apache-2.0**

[Quick start](#quick-start) · [The name](#the-story-behind-the-name) · [Why HelixHarness](#why-helixharness) · [Framework iteration platform](#a-platform-for-iterating-on-helixharness) · [User guide](docs/user-guide.md)

## The story behind the name

Every team has its own way of building software: the business rules it protects, the architecture it works within, the checks it trusts and the lessons it has learned. Together, these form its **engineering DNA**.

**Helix** evokes the DNA double helix: knowledge carried forward and refined over time. **Harness** gives that knowledge a role in execution—the context, constraints and workflow that guide a coding agent through real project work.

Born from engineering practice in Didi's financial technology team, HelixHarness brings these ideas together. Project knowledge and rules help it adapt to your team; verified lessons retained at Archive give later tasks a stronger starting point. For framework maintainers, observations and controlled evaluations inform the next change, with adoption kept in human hands.

**The code ships. The knowledge stays. The harness evolves.**

## Why HelixHarness

| Capability | What it means in your project |
| --- | --- |
| **A Harness grounded in your project** | Repository instructions and indexed project constraints give the agent concrete engineering rules to follow during planning and implementation. |
| **Knowledge that compounds** | Stable, verified business rules, interface boundaries and implementation lessons can be recorded at Archive after your confirmation, then reused in later tasks. |
| **Context loaded when needed** | Harness and knowledge indexes guide which documents to load for the current requirement, task or archive step. The agent revisits context as the work changes. |
| **An inspectable development lifecycle** | Propose defines scope and acceptance; Apply implements, tests and reviews; Archive checks completion and records the outcome. Specs, tasks and evidence remain in the repository. |
| **Continuity across sessions and repositories** | Persisted workflow state supports resuming unfinished work. A multi-repo Workspace records repository responsibilities and coordinates work across services. |

Here, **Harness** means the project constraints and execution rules that guide the agent: what to read, which boundaries to respect and what evidence is required to finish. See the [context loading protocol](helixharness/reference/loading-protocol.md).

Development workflow: project constraints and knowledge guide Propose and Apply; Archive retains verified knowledge after confirmation

### Your engineering DNA, made actionable

**Turn team experience into context your agent can use.** HelixHarness organizes project knowledge, engineering constraints, requirements and checks alongside your code, so they can be reviewed, reused and updated as the project evolves.

| Part | The question it answers | Where it lives in your project |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Knowledge · Project understanding** | How does this system work? Which business rules and past decisions matter? | `docs/knowledge/` |
| **Harness · Engineering constraints** | Which development rules and architectural boundaries must the agent respect? | `docs/harness/` |
| **Specs · Task contracts** | What are we building, and what evidence will demonstrate completion? | `docs/specs/` |
| **Hooks · Checks and gates** | Which checks apply at key execution and review stages? | `docs/hooks/` and host hook configuration |

Knowledge and Harness indexes guide context loading. Specs hold each task's scope, plan and verification evidence. Hooks combine host runtime hooks, workflow gates and review checklists; their execution depends on the host and workflow configuration. See the [context loading protocol](helixharness/reference/loading-protocol.md) and [hook setup](docs/installation.md).

### What knowledge reuse looks like

Suppose a refund feature establishes a state transition rule and a cross-service interface boundary. After implementation and verification, Archive proposes the stable knowledge to retain, and you confirm the update. When the next refund-related feature starts, Propose and Apply can load that knowledge through the index, giving the agent an existing project reference to work from.

Knowledge accumulates as **reviewable repository documents**. You control what becomes shared project knowledge.

**Start with the plugin alone.** It works independently of the platform. The [task-filter example](examples/README.md) includes a starter project, a requirement and an independent acceptance check.

## Quick start

### 1. Install the plugin

Requirements: Python 3.10+, Git and a plugin-capable Codex or Claude Code installation. Make sure the host is signed in or has its model configuration set up and is working normally.

After the repository is public, run the commands for your host in a terminal. No manual source clone is needed:

```bash
# Codex
codex plugin marketplace add https://github.com/didi/helixharness.git
codex plugin add helix@helixharness-marketplace
```

```bash
# Claude Code
claude plugin marketplace add https://github.com/didi/helixharness.git
claude plugin install helix@helixharness-marketplace
```

The root marketplace installs the `helixharness/` plugin, not the platform. For testing before publication or modifying the plugin, use [developer installation from local source](docs/installation.md#developer-installation). See [hook verification, updates and uninstall](docs/installation.md).

### 2. Run a small feature

The product name is **HelixHarness**; its plugin ID and command namespace are **`helix`**.

Open a new agent session in the **application repository** you want to develop. Review the plugin hooks through the host's native interface, then enter these commands in the conversation:

```text
/helix:init
/helix:propose task-filter ./requirements/task-filter.md --loop
```

Use the [self-contained task-filter example](examples/README.md) to get a starter project, requirement and acceptance check. `--loop` runs Propose → Apply → Archive, pausing for decisions or blockers. It does not publish or deploy your code.

You can also run `/helix:propose`, `/helix:apply` and `/helix:archive` separately. See [all nine commands](docs/user-guide.md#commands).

Use `/helix:status` to inspect progress and blockers, and `/helix:config` to view or change telemetry consent and reporting addresses.

## How it relates to Superpowers and OpenSpec

These projects offer useful, overlapping approaches to agent-assisted development. This comparison highlights their emphasis:

| Project | Emphasis |
| --- | --- |
| [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) | Composable development skills and practices: brainstorming, planning, TDD, subagent execution and code review. |
| [OpenSpec](https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec) | Specification-driven change management: align on proposals, specs, design and tasks, then implement and archive changes. |
| **HelixHarness** | Bring project Harness constraints and reusable knowledge into the development lifecycle, with an optional platform to observe, evaluate and improve the framework itself. |

See [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) for attribution and related work.

## A platform for iterating on HelixHarness

**helixharness-platform serves maintainers who change HelixHarness's commands, workflow rules, skills and context-loading strategies.** It connects usage evidence, controlled version comparisons and candidate improvements into a framework iteration process.

| Capability | The question it helps answer | What you can inspect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Observability** | Where does HelixHarness encounter friction in actual use? | Workflow execution records, stage status, time and Token usage, rework and evidence quality. |
| **Evaluation** | Does this change improve the HelixHarness framework? | Frozen Base and Candidate versions exercised against the same Cases; inspect results, regression gates and execution evidence. |
| **Evolution** | Which framework change is worth testing next? | Evidence-backed hypotheses, isolated candidate changes and frozen experiments; review the proposal and decide whether to adopt the result. |

**The evaluation target is the HelixHarness framework version or change.** Development scenarios exercise that framework, and their outcomes provide evidence about its behavior. This platform supports framework iteration; it is not a general service for grading the business code HelixHarness generates.

Framework iteration: observe, hypothesize, build a candidate, evaluate, review and adopt, then observe again

### Three views of framework iteration

     Observability
     Evaluation
     Evolution

     Locate workflow friction and resource usage.
     Inspect a controlled framework version comparison.
     Inspect the evidence loop and evolution overview.

Click any screenshot to enlarge it. All three show the real platform UI with **synthetic demonstration data**. Evaluation uses Mock execution; the evolution view shows the evidence loop and synthetic evidence summary. These are interface examples, not measured improvements or real model results.

Real evaluation requires your own model service and calibrated Cases. Evolution proposals and candidate changes remain reviewable; adopting and publishing a framework change requires human decisions.

### Try the platform Demo

Download or clone the source first, then run these commands from the combined repository root:

```bash
# From the combined repository root
cd helixharness-platform
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e '.[server]'
python -m web_ui.demo --port 7860
```

Open [localhost:7860](http://127.0.0.1:7860). The Demo generates synthetic Case, Mock Run and telemetry data from bundled source examples in a temporary runtime directory. Generated databases, acceptance-test Runs and candidate workspaces are not included in the source or wheel. Background evolution and model analysis are disabled. The built-in Demo does not generate evolution hypotheses; the evolution screenshot shows the overview without generated hypotheses or candidates.

## Repository map

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`helixharness/`](helixharness/README.md) | Agent plugin, workflow commands, host adapters and runtime tests |
| [`helixharness-platform/`](helixharness-platform/README.md) | Optional observability, evaluation and evolution for the HelixHarness framework |
| [`examples/`](examples/README.md) | Reproducible starter project and observable acceptance criteria |
| [`docs/`](docs/user-guide.md) | Configuration, workflows, troubleshooting and verification boundaries |

It locates the plugin independently in each frozen commit, supporting standalone, combined and nested monorepo layouts. Multiple plugin copies require an explicit Git-relative path; no nested Git repository is required. [Evaluation setup](docs/user-guide.md#version-evaluation).

# 🌟 核心功能

## 🤖 真能干活的机器人

机器人不只是一个聊天窗口：它有自己的人设、默认模型、工作区和记忆。

- **想建几个就建几个**，每个都有自己的人设、模型、工作区和头像。
- **它是谁由你写。** 人设就是一段话，模板只是起点，每个字都能改；六个头像只管长相，不决定它能做什么。
- **真正的文件操作。** 机器人能读写文件、在沙箱里执行命令，并把结果作为文件发回聊天。
- **每个机器人三档权限。** *只读*、*工作区*（默认：只能写自己的文件夹，越界先问你）、*完全权限*（不进沙箱；递归删除仍会先问）。
- **审批卡片，没有意外。** 越界的操作会停下来，等你回答。
- **重启了也会告诉你。** 应用退出或崩溃时还没处理完的消息，下次启动会在原对话里说一声，请你重新发送，不会自动重做。
- **斜杠命令**，如 `/model`、`/reset`，在应用和各个聊天渠道里都能用；在聊天渠道里发 `/bot` 可以换机器人。

## ⏳ 在后台干活，需要你时才来找你

- **后台任务。** 要跑一阵子的事（调研、做报告、整理文件），或者你说一句「后台做」，机器人会开一个后台任务，你可以接着聊别的。做完把结果发回原来的对话。
- **接着问。** 在微信里引用结果、在飞书里回复那条消息，就是继续问这个任务。
- **规则。** 「每天早上 8 点看看 X 的价格，低于 200 告诉我」会建成一条规则，到点就去查，有值得说的才告诉你。想先看看它会怎么做，就说「先观察」：只记下本会说什么，不发消息、不改文件，看过几次再改成执行。
- **「需要你」。** 所有机器人在等你回答、批准或重试的事都在侧栏这一行里；没事时这一行不出现。信息面板的「任务」组列着这个机器人的任务和规则，每一步都看得到。
- **不吵你。** 只推结果、要你决定的事和失败，进展不推。默认 22:00 到 08:00 免打扰；主动消息每天有上限（微信 3 条，其他渠道 5 条），多了合成一条。
- **有预算。** 每个任务、每条规则都有预算（任务默认 1 美元，规则每次 0.1 美元、每月 3 美元），快用完时停下问你，可以在任务详情和规则编辑器里改。
- **随时暂停。** 机器人设置 › 主动消息里一个开关暂停后台工作，聊天照常。
- **用完会清理。** 任务和运行记录留 30 天；任务文件夹 30 天没动过会自动删除，不来问你，任务详情里写着哪天删，想留就点保留。运行记录能导出成 Markdown。

完整介绍见[《AnyModelBot 超级智能体》](./docs/blog/superagent.md)。

## 🖥️ 操作你的电脑，生成图片和视频

- **电脑操作**由内置的 [Cua Driver](https://github.com/trycua/cua) 提供。默认自动执行；把某个机器人切到「改变界面前先问我」，每一次点击和输入都要等你点头。读取屏幕内容永远不需要审批。macOS 上的电脑操作是 Beta 功能。
- **图片和视频生成**直接生成，要求没说清的按最合理的理解来；预计花费超过 0.5 美元时才先问你，让你看到模型和提示词，也可以当场换模型。想每次都确认，在机器人设置里打开即可。

## 🌐 任意模型，通过 Modelflare

- **登录一次**，你的 Modelflare 模型就会自动出现。更想用 Key？直接粘贴也行。
- **一个选择器，覆盖所有模型。** GPT、Claude、Gemini、Grok、DeepSeek、Kimi、GLM 等，每个都标出上下文长度、能力和参考价。
- **按对话切换**，也可以给每个机器人设默认模型；记忆整理、上下文交接这类后台小任务，还能单独指定一个模型。
- **两条线路。** 国际线路和中国大陆优化线路，由你自己选，AnyModelBot 不会自动来回切换。
- **按量付费。** 钱包余额、低余额提醒、每日用量、每个机器人的预算 Key 都内置。AnyModelBot 没有订阅。

## 🧠 有记忆，随处可达

- **记忆会延续。** 机器人用 Markdown 保存三层记忆（团队、机器人、群），会过滤看起来像密钥的内容。
- **长对话也能用下去。** 上下文快满之前，上下文管家会压缩，或开一个新段并带上交接摘要。
- **账号全局共用。** 微信、飞书、Telegram、Slack、Discord、Notion 的账号在设置里加一次，所有机器人共用，每个服务可以加多个、起别名。在聊天软件里发一次 `/bot 名字` 就换一个机器人聊，也可以让机器人读你的 Notion 和飞书消息。
- **微信和飞书。** 微信扫码连接，飞书机器人支持流式回复卡片；微信还能收发图片和文件。
- **Telegram、Slack、Discord。** 在 设置 › 连接 里填 token 连接，不需要公网地址；回复边写边显示，能收发图片和文件。目前只处理单聊，审批和提问回复文字。
- **四种运行方式。** 桌面版、命令行、Docker，以及 `127.0.0.1:3600` 的本地网页控制台。

## 🔒 本地优先，也好看

- **数据留在你手里。** 对话、记忆、文件和 API Key 都存放在你的设备上。本地控制台只监听 `127.0.0.1`，桌面版每次启动都会生成新的访问令牌。
- **只听主人的。** 机器人默认只回应主人（扫码登录的微信；飞书、Telegram、Slack、Discord 连上后第一个给它发消息的人，也就是你）和你允许的人。其他人发消息只会收到一句提示，不会调用模型；你在信息面板里，或在聊天里回复「同意 编号」放行。
- **回复不会丢。** 回复先存到本地再发；网络断了会自动重试，应用重启后接着发；你在微信里超过 24 小时没说话时，回复先留着，等你下次发消息时一起送到。
- **遥测保持关闭。** 内置电脑操作驱动的遥测已关闭，内置网关以关闭自动更新的方式运行。
- **浅色、深色或跟随系统。** 六个机器人角色，眼睛会跟着你的鼠标转。
- **托盘与开机自启。** 关闭窗口会收到托盘；macOS 和 Windows 支持开机自启。

> [!NOTE]
> 功能是否可用取决于你选择的模型、操作系统和授予的权限。电脑操作需要桌面会话，macOS 上的电脑操作为 Beta。模型请求会经过 Modelflare 转发给你选定的供应商，详见[工作原理与隐私](#-工作原理与隐私)。

# 🆚 对比 Grok Bot / OpenAI dots / Claude Duet

2026 年下半年，xAI 的 [Grok Bot](https://x.ai/bot)、OpenAI 的 [dots](https://openai.com/index/introducing-dots/) 和 Anthropic 的 Claude Duet 接连发布，"常驻的个人 AI 智能体"成了热门：它替你盯着事情、在后台干活，需要你决定时再来找你。AnyModelBot 做的是同一类事，换了一种做法：开源、跑在你自己的设备上、任意模型都能用。

| | AnyModelBot | Grok Bot | OpenAI dots | Claude Duet |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 开源 | ✅ MIT | — | — | — |
| 智能体跑在哪 | 你自己的电脑或服务器 | xAI 的云端电脑 | OpenAI 的云端电脑 | Anthropic 的云端 |
| 能用的模型 | GPT、Claude、Gemini、Grok、DeepSeek、Kimi、GLM 等 70+ 个（经 Modelflare） | 以 xAI 的 Grok 模型为主 | OpenAI 的模型 | Claude（Opus 5.5） |
| 费用 | 应用免费，模型按 token 计费 | 订阅 | ChatGPT Pro / Business Premium 订阅 | Claude Pro / Max 订阅 |
| 在哪找它 | 桌面应用（Windows、macOS、Linux）、Docker、微信、飞书、Telegram、Slack、Discord | 桌面应用、iPhone | ChatGPT、Slack、Teams | iOS、Android、claude.ai |
| 现在能用吗 | 直接下载 | 测试版 | 部分地区开放 | 研究预览，美国候补名单 |

AnyModelBot 同样能在后台干活：交代的任务可以在后台跑完，再把结果发到你用的聊天渠道；需要你批准或回答时，它会出现在侧栏的「需要你」里。机器人做的每一步都看得见，越出工作区的操作先问你。

> [!NOTE]
> 其他产品的信息来自 2026 年 10 月的公开报道，可能已有变化，以各家官方说明为准。Grok Bot、dots、Claude Duet 分别是 xAI、OpenAI、Anthropic 的产品和商标，AnyModelBot 与它们没有关联。

# 🔐 工作原理与隐私

| 留在你的设备上 | 会离开你的设备 |
| :--- | :--- |
| 对话与会话（本地 SQLite 数据库） | 模型回答所需的提示词、文件内容和工具结果，经 Modelflare 发给你选定的供应商 |
| 记忆（Markdown 文件） | 你让机器人用电脑操作看屏幕时的屏幕截图 |
| 每个机器人工作区里的文件 | 你通过聊天渠道收发的消息，会经过对应的平台 |
| 你的 API Key 和登录令牌 | 你登录 Modelflare 的过程，发生在 modelflare.dev |
| 设置 | 你添加 Notion 或飞书账号后，机器人会读写这些账号的内容，读到的内容也会进入模型请求 |

Modelflare 会保留请求日志；保留什么、保留多久，见它的[信任中心](https://modelflare.dev/trust?utm_source=anymodelbot&utm_campaign=amb_readme)。我们不声称能做到万无一失：凡是你发给模型的内容，都会离开你的设备。完整清单见 [docs/privacy.md](./docs/privacy.md)。

| 层 | 技术 |
| :--- | :--- |
| 界面 | Preact + htm，无构建步骤 |
| 后端 | Node.js 22.13+、TypeScript、`node:sqlite` |
| 桌面外壳 | Electron，带托盘 |
| 模型网关 | [magpie](https://github.com/yetone/magpie)（Go，MIT），随应用打包并由应用启动 |
| 智能体运行时 | [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)（MIT），作为独立进程运行 |
| 电脑操作 | [Cua Driver](https://github.com/trycua/cua)，随应用打包 |
| 渠道 | 飞书（长连接 + 流式卡片）、微信（iLink）、Telegram（长轮询）、Slack（Socket Mode）、Discord（Gateway） |
| 数据账号 | Notion（REST API、官方远程 MCP）、飞书消息（用户身份，只读） |
| 测试与 CI | Vitest、GitHub Actions |

# 📝 路线图

我们正在探索的方向。它们不是承诺，顺序也不是排期。每个版本实际改了什么，见[更新日志](./CHANGELOG.md)。

- [x] **定时任务**：让机器人按时间表自己干活（已上线，就是上面的规则）。
- [ ] **群聊**：目前各聊天渠道只处理一对一对话。
- [x] **英文界面**：已支持中英双语，在设置里切换。
- [ ] **macOS 电脑操作**：在更多真机上验证 direct 模式，让它脱离 Beta。
- [ ] **邮箱、日历和事件触发**：接入邮箱和日历账号，规则除了按时间跑，也能在事情发生时马上跑（比如收到某人的邮件、快开会时）。由外部内容触发的运行权限更低，防止别人写的内容给机器人下指令。
- [ ] **常驻运行、备份和迁移**：电脑关机时规则不会跑。让普通用户也能一键部署到自己的服务器，把对话、记忆和账号搬过去，也能备份和恢复。
- [ ] **自己添加 MCP**：目前只能用内置的工具和账号。开放后，可以自己接入 GitHub、Linear 等服务。
- [ ] **机器人之间协作**：让一个机器人把活交给另一个，比如用不同的模型写稿和审稿，花费分开算。
- [ ] **语音消息转写**：Telegram 的语音消息目前听不到内容，微信靠平台自带的转写。
- [ ] **独立的手机应用**：目前可以从微信、飞书、Telegram、Slack、Discord 找到你的机器人。

有别的想法？欢迎提 [issue](https://github.com/modelflare-ai/AnyModelBot/issues) 或发起[讨论](https://github.com/modelflare-ai/AnyModelBot/discussions)。我们决定要做的事项，会用 [`roadmap`](https://github.com/modelflare-ai/AnyModelBot/labels/roadmap) 标签跟踪。

# 🐸 rainfrog

a database tool for the terminal

rainfrog demo

[![Crate Badge]][Crate] [![Repo Badge]][Repo] [![License Badge]](./LICENSE) \
[![CI Badge]][CI] [Built With Ratatui](https://ratatui.rs/)

## features

the goal for rainfrog is to provide a lightweight, terminal-based tool for
interacting with databases.
- efficient navigation via vim-like keybindings and mouse controls
- query editor with keyword highlighting, session history, and favorites
- quickly copy data, filter tables, and switch between schemas
- shortcuts to view table metadata and properties
- cross-platform (macOS, linux, windows, android via termux)

### why "rainfrog"?

> [frogs find refuge in elephant tracks](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2019/06/190604131157.htm)

### supported databases

the levels of support for different databases can be split into 4 tiers:
- **tier 1**: most frequently tested, bugs will be addressed as soon as possible.
- **tier 2**: often tested, fixed when necessary.
- **tier 3**: community supported; contributions are welcome, but otherwise development is minimal.
- **tier 4**: new or experimental; should be treated as unstable, and behavior is subject to change.

| database | tier | known issues | via wire protocol* |
| -------- | ---- | ------------ | ------------------ |
| postgres | 1 |  | |
| mysql | 2 |  | |
| sqlite | 2  |          | |
| redshift | 2 |          | postgres |
| duckdb | 2 | prebuilt android, i686, and musl binaries do not include this driver      | |
| oracle | 3 | requires additional runtime dependencies          | |

*the postgres driver can also be used to connect to other databases that support
the postgres wire protocol, such as AWS Redshift. however, this functionality is not
well tested. in theory, the mysql driver should be able to do the same for databases
that support the mysql protocol. check each database's documentation for compatibility.

## disclaimer

this software is currently under active development; expect breaking changes,
and use at your own risk. it is not recommended to use this tool with write
access on a production database.

## installation

### cargo

after installing rust (recommended to do so via
[rustup](https://www.rust-lang.org/tools/install)):

```sh
cargo install rainfrog --locked
```

by default, all features are included. some features may not be compatible with your platform;
check [Cargo.toml](./Cargo.toml) to see what feature combinations are available.

if you have [cargo-binstall](https://github.com/cargo-bins/cargo-binstall), you can run:
```sh
cargo binstall rainfrog
```

### homebrew
```sh
brew install rainfrog
```

### arch linux

arch linux users can install from the
[official repositories](https://archlinux.org/packages/extra/x86_64/rainfrog)
using [pacman](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/pacman):

```sh
pacman -S rainfrog
```

### termux

if you are using [termux](https://termux.dev/), you'll need to install rust via
their package manager:

```sh
pkg install rust
```

and then make sure to install with termux features (and disable default
features):

```sh
cargo install rainfrog --no-default-features
```

### nix

```sh
nix-env -iA nixos.rainfrog
```

### conda

```sh
conda install -c conda-forge rainfrog
```

### pixi

The command below installs rainfrog from conda-forge, the same repository as conda, but unlike conda it can be installed user-globally using [pixi](https://pixi.sh/).

```sh
pixi global install rainfrog
```

### install script

there is a simple install script that assists in downloading and unpacking a
binary from the release page to `~/.local/bin/`, which you might want to add to
your `PATH` variable if it isn't already there. you'll need to select which
binary is appropriate for your system (if you're not sure, you can find out by
installing rust and running `rustc -vV` to see the "host" target), and the
script also needs [jq](https://github.com/jqlang/jq) and
[fzf](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf) installed to run.

```sh
curl -LSsf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/achristmascarl/rainfrog/main/install.sh | bash
```

### release page binaries

1. manually download and unpack the appropriate binary for your os from the
   latest [release](https://github.com/achristmascarl/rainfrog/releases) (if
   you're not sure which binary to pick, you can find out by installing rust and
   running `rustc -vV` to see the "host" target)
2. move the binary to a folder in your `PATH` environment variable

### icons
you will need to have a nerd font installed and used by your terminal for the icons to show up.

## dependencies
for some of the databases supported by rainfrog, the driver has additional runtime dependencies.
you can find instructions for installing those dependencies below.

### oracle
the oracle driver uses ODPI-C, which requires Oracle Client libraries to be installed. instructions
for installing the Oracle Instant Client can be found here: [ODPI-C Installation](https://odpi-c.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/installation.html).

after installation, you may need to manually copy the client files to a
location where ODPI-C can find them, which is either in the same folder as the rainfrog binary,
or in the library path of your os. more details can be found in the ODPI-C
installation instructions: [ODPI-C Client Library Loading](https://odpi-c.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/installation.html#oracle-client-library-loading).

## usage

```sh
Usage: rainfrog [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  edit  Edit the config file (create it first if missing)
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -M, --mouse         Whether to enable mouse event support. If enabled, your terminal's
                                 default mouse event handling will not work. [possible values: true,
                                 false]
  -u, --url                  Full connection URL for the database, e.g.
                                 postgres://username:password@localhost:5432/dbname
      --username        Username for database connection
      --password        Password for database connection
  -R, --reenter-password         Reenter the password for a saved database connection
      --host                Host for database connection (ex. localhost)
      --port                Port for database connection (ex. 5432)
      --database        Name of database for connection (ex. postgres)
      --driver            Driver for database connection (ex. postgres)
      --enable-cleartext-plugin  Enable MySQL cleartext plugin
      --ssl-required             Require an SSL/TLS connection (supported by PostgreSQL, MySQL, and
                                 Oracle)
  -h, --help                     Print help
  -V, --version                  Print version
```

### with connection options

if any options are not provided, you will be prompted to input them.
if you do not provide an input, that option will
default to what is in your environment variables.

```sh
rainfrog \
  --driver   \
  --username   \
  --host   \
  --port   \
  --database   \
  --ssl-required
```

### with connection url

the `connection_url` must include all the necessary options for connecting
to the database (ex. `postgres://username:password@localhost:5432/postgres`).
it will take precedence over all connection options.

```sh
rainfrog --url $(connection_url) --ssl-required
```

`--ssl-required` overrides the transport setting from a connection URL. It selects
PostgreSQL's `require` mode, MySQL's `required` mode, or Oracle's `tcps` protocol.
SQLite and DuckDB do not support SSL/TLS connections. Advanced certificate and
verification settings can still be supplied in PostgreSQL and MySQL URL parameters,
or through an Oracle Easy Connect string and Oracle client configuration.

### with environment variables
if `connection_url` is not present, rainfrog will first check your `DATABASE_URL`
environment variable, then it will check for `DATABASE_URL` in a `.env` file in
the current directory or a parent directory.

### `docker run`

for postgres and mysql, you can run it by specifying all
of the options as environment variables:

```sh
docker run --platform linux/amd64 -it --rm --name rainfrog \
  --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
  -e db_driver="db_driver" \
  -e username=" " \
  -e password=" " \
  -e hostname="host.docker.internal" \
  -e db_port=" " \
  -e db_name=" " achristmascarl/rainfrog:latest
```

if you want to provide a custom combination of
options and omit others, you can override the Dockerfile's
CMD like so:

```sh
docker run --platform linux/amd64 -it --rm --name rainfrog \
  achristmascarl/rainfrog:latest \
  rainfrog # overrides CMD, additional options would come after
```

since sqlite is file-based, you may need to mount a path to
the sqlite db as a volume in order to access it:

```sh
docker run --platform linux/amd64 -it --rm --name rainfrog \
  -v ~/code/rainfrog/dev/rainfrog.sqlite3:/rainfrog.sqlite3 \
  achristmascarl/rainfrog:latest \
  rainfrog --url sqlite:///rainfrog.sqlite3
```

running drivers which have runtime dependencies (like oracle) via docker
is not currently supported.

## customization

rainfrog can be customized by placing a `rainfrog_config.toml` file in
one of the following locations depending on your os, as determined by
the [directories](https://crates.io/crates/directories) crate:

| Platform | Value                                                                   | Example                                                       |

# EVOLV — the self-evolving AI workspace that rewrites itself

**EVOLV is a self-evolving AI agent workspace: a self-modifying coding agent that grows its own UI, tools, skills, prompts and plugins live while you watch.** Local-first, single Go binary, works with Ollama or any API key — and the demo below needs none.

[GitHub stars](https://github.com/dxn111/EVOLV/stargazers)
[CI](https://github.com/dxn111/EVOLV/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[License: MIT](LICENSE)
[Release](https://github.com/dxn111/EVOLV/releases)

**No API key. No signup. One command.**

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dxn111/EVOLV/main/install.sh | sh
```

```bash
$ evolv          # boots on localhost:7373, opens your browser
```

[▶ **watch the full video (mp4)**](docs/assets/demo.mp4) — no edits, real stream

---

## What you just watched

That GIF wasn't scripted. You're looking at an AI **rewriting its own application while it runs**:

1. A human asked for a pomodoro timer.
2. The agent didn't paste code back. It **wrote a real component into its own source tree** (`~/.evolv/workspace/ui/components/pomodoro.html`) and logged the change in an append-only evolution ledger.
3. A filesystem watcher caught the write the instant it happened and pushed it over WebSocket — the new panel appeared **in the conversation itself, with no refresh, no rebuild, no restart**.
4. Then it grew a playable **Flappy Bird** the same way. The whole page is the canvas — every component mounts inline where it was born, and any organ can be opened **across the entire window** from the sidebar.

The app you installed is not the app you're running five minutes later.

> Most "AI workspaces" give you a chat window with plugins someone else wrote.
> EVOLV *is* the chat window — and it writes its own plugins, its own UI, and its own mind.

### Part 2: it edits its own codebase — and you see it in real time

Components are just the surface. The second demo asks the organism to **rewrite its own source**:

[▶ **watch the full video (mp4)**](docs/assets/selfedit.mp4) — the agent edits its own `index.html` and `style.css`, forces its own recompile (watch the RECOMPILING SHELL overlay), and keeps going. In the same session it also:

- **grew a Prompt Library button** — template cards that drop into the composer — plus the skill for using it (one batch, two mutations);
- **installed `ghost-log`, a live plugin** in its own sandbox that pops a toast every time the organism mutates;
- **grew a playable Flappy Bird** onto its canvas. A video game, written by the app into itself, live:

And the overlay shot — the app flashing "RECOMPILING SHELL · agent requested a shell recompile" *because the agent asked it to*:

  More views of the organism

  the shell at boot: quiet, warm, no neon

  the genome inspector: every file of the body, editable live

---

## Why this is different

| | Traditional AI chat | Plugin-based workspace | **EVOLV** |
|---|---|---|---|
| UI | fixed | fixed | **self-rewriting, hot-reloaded** |
| Tools | prebuilt | marketplace | **grown at runtime, compiled live** |
| Skills / prompts | frozen | frozen | **self-edited, versioned in a ledger** |
| New feature request | "here's some code you could paste…" | "wait for the dev" | **materialized on your canvas in seconds** |
| Improvement loop | ends when the chat ends | manual | **continuous, visible, alive** |

### It edits itself. It edits YOUR code.

EVOLV is not a walled-garden canvas. It is a **full agent workspace** with the whole machine as its hands:

- **Own body, every byte.** Its chat shell, its CSS skin, its tool call cards, its front-brain JS, its panels — all plain files it rewrites live. Say *"make your tool call cards look exactly like Claude's"* and it opens its own `style.css`, rewrites the card section, reloads its shell — and the new skin lands in under a second, no refresh.
- **Even the launcher.** If the EVOLV source tree is on the machine, it detects it and can read and edit its own Go kernel (`cmd/`, `internal/`) — the code that runs it. Then `go build ./cmd/evolv`. A program that patches its own bootloader.
- **Your projects.** Point it at any folder (*"work on the project at ~/my-app"*, or `set_project`): it reads, edits, runs tests and ships code there like any serious coding agent — while still being the workspace it lives in.

### Zero refresh. Ever. You see every change as it happens.

- **Skin hot-swap** — when the agent (or you) rewrites `style.css`, the new skin slides in **without a reload and without a flash**. The organism changes clothes while you're looking at it.
- **Genome Inspector** — the 🗂 button opens every file of the body in a live modal: watch the file list flicker as the agent mutates (changed files flash green), open anything, edit it, hit ctrl+s. Your write lands in the genome like one of the agent's own — same watcher, same live effect.
- **The Mind panel** — the sidebar shows every skill, tool, plugin and prompt the organism currently carries, updating the instant something grows.
- **Shell recompiles** (index.html / app.js) still show the "RECOMPILING SHELL" overlay — a 900ms morph, not a reload.

### A body that doesn't embarrass itself

The default skin is a quiet, Claude-grade warm dark theme — no neon cyberpunk, no particle noise, no emoji confetti. Chat looks like chat: your messages right-aligned in soft bubbles, the agent's answers as clean prose, tool calls as calm bordered cards with a single green check. There is no separate "canvas pane" — **the whole page is the canvas**: components the organism grows mount inline in the conversation, and the ⤢ control (or the Organs list in the sidebar) opens any organ across the entire window. And since the skin is just `workspace/ui/style.css`, the organism can still restyle every pixel of this while it runs — that's the point.

### Plugins that are actually alive

Plugins aren't dead scripts — each one runs in **its own sandbox with a real-time nervous system**:

```js
// workspace/plugins/ /plugin.js — this is running, now
evolv.on("evolution", (e) => evolv.log("saw a mutation:", e.kind, e.name));
evolv.on("agent:token", (e) => { /* react to every streamed token */ });
evolv.every(30000, () => evolv.log("heartbeat — still alive"));
evolv.toast("hello from inside the organism");
```

`evolv.on` fires the moment the event happens on the bus — mutations, streamed tokens, phase changes, fs changes, dreams. The repo ships a `pulse` plugin so you can watch it work immediately.

### Time travel: every state of the organism is kept

Before **every mutation batch** the whole genome is frozen into `~/.evolv/snapshots/` (the last 20 states are kept). The agent can freeze and rewind itself mid-conversation:

```
{"action":"snapshot"}                       → "genome frozen — restore anytime"
{"action":"rollback","path":"latest"}       → the whole organism rewinds, live
```

Rolled back a bad evolution and instantly regretted it? Snapshots are also exposed in the UI/API (`/api/snapshots`), so *you* can time-travel the organism too.

### Dream mode: it evolves itself while you're away

Flip on **Dream mode** in Settings (or press the *💭 dream now* button). When the organism has been idle for the heartbeat interval, it wakes up **on its own**, reviews its own body — skills, prompts, tools, its own skin — grows one real improvement, and rolls over back to sleep. You come back to a chat that quietly says:

> 💭 dreamed while you were away. I taught myself deep-work.

Every dream is a real conversation turn, so the organism *remembers its dreams* — and every dream is snapshotted first, so nightmares are one rollback away.

### Swarm mode: many minds, one organism

Open **`/swarm`** (the 🐝 button in the sidebar) to convene a colony of **5–100 agents** across five roles: **Ideators** propose directions, **Coders** build the chosen one, **Testers** try to break it, **Critics** argue with both, and **Judges** write the final decision. They share one transcript, work in phases, and settle decisions with explicit **polls** — every agent casts a vote with a reason. Votes are collected in one call per role cohort, so a 100-agent poll costs five model calls instead of a hundred.

If the ship poll says **revise**, the coders apply the critique and the testers retest before the judge closes the run. The page streams live `swarm:activity`, `swarm:state` and poll bars over the existing WebSocket, filters the roster by role, exports the whole run as Markdown, and restores the last run from `workspace/swarm/last.json` after a restart. Terminal runs are archived under `workspace/swarm/runs/` and reopen from the run picker.

You are in the room too: **type while the colony is working to steer it**, and **click vote on an open poll** to add your own ballot. A live colony map and phase rail show where the 5–100 agents are. `POST /api/swarm` starts a run (`agents` 5–100); `POST /api/swarm/steer` adds a human message; `POST /api/swarm/vote` casts your vote; `/api/swarm/stop` cancels. Beta, and honest about it: artifacts are proposals until a tester actually runs them.

### The full action list

| Action | What it does |
|---|---|
| `set_plan` / `plan_advance` / `complete_task` | persistent task state, one-call progress, and a structured completion report |
| `evolve_component` | mounts a new live UI panel mid-conversation |
| `evolve_tool` / `run_tool` / `list_tools` | compiles a JS tool into its sandbox, with an optional typed argument schema |
| `evolve_skill` / `evolve_prompt` | grows its own playbooks and system prompt |
| `evolve_plugin` | installs a **live** plugin: own sandbox, reacts to bus events via `evolv.on`, real timers via `evolv.every` |
| `write_file` / `edit_file` / `read_file` | any file, any path on your machine (hash-guarded writes) |
| `list_dir` / `tree` / `map_repo` / `move` / `delete_file` | filesystem navigation plus a cached Go/JS/TS repository outline |
| `run_tests` / `set_project` / `shell` | auto-detected test suites, project binding, commands (120s timeout) |
| `snapshot` / `rollback` | time travel: freeze the genome, rewind the whole organism |
| `stage_candidate` / `list_candidates` / `promote_candidate` | isolated, hash-pinned kernel proposals with an explicit promotion gate |
| `self_modify` / `self_update` | compile, test and stage a kernel candidate, or morph to the latest release |
| `reload_shell` | forces the browser to recompile its UI now |

Every mutation is logged to `workspace/evolution.jsonl` and streamed to your screen as it happens. And you can play too: **the body is plain files.** Edit anything in `~/.evolv/workspace/` — it hot-reloads.

---

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dxn111/EVOLV/main/install.sh | sh
```

The installer detects your OS/arch, downloads the prebuilt binary (or builds from source if needed), puts `evolv` on your PATH, and prints a launch card. Check what it would install first with `install.sh --version`, or pin a release with `EVOLV_VERSION=v0.22.0 install.sh`.

**Full documentation:** [docs/index.html](docs/index.html) — a single-page guide generated straight from this README (`go run ./cmd/evolv-docs`), plus the [24-hour master plan](docs/EVOLV-24H-MASTERPLAN.md).

  Other ways in

```bash
# with Go toolchain
go install github.com/dxn111/EVOLV/evolv@latest

# from source
git clone https://github.com/dxn111/EVOLV
cd EVOLV && make install

# grab a binary from Releases
# macOS / Linux / Windows (amd64 + arm64) — see github.com/dxn111/EVOLV/releases
```

Then:

```bash
evolv                  # → http://localhost:7373 opens in your browser automatically
evolv update           # morph in-place to the latest release (genome survives)
evolv update --check   # current vs latest, no download
evolv download         # fetch the latest platform binary into this folder
evolv status           # live health card for a running organism
evolv --port 8080      # custom port
evolv --no-open        # head

Start with the [repository map](L1.md) and [development guide](docs/DEV_GUIDE.md)

corepack enable
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm typecheck
pnpm lint

cp .dev.vars.example .dev.vars

Forks must configure their own Cloudflare Worker, D1 database, R2 buckets,
email sender, Turnstile widget, OAuth applications, domains, and secrets.
Never commit credentials, private packages, or licensed runtime files.
